title: Travel: Paul and Linda McCartney – London to Lagos | 1973
content:
Paul and Linda McCartney flew to Lagos with their children on 30 August 1973.

Wings had decided to record their third album in the Nigerian capital. EMI had agreed to let them use their studio in the city, and Denny Laine and engineer Geoff Emerick had flown there the previous day.

The trip got off to a bad start. The band’s guitarist Henry McCullough had recently walked out, and their drummer Denny Seiwell had quit the day before.

Amateurish isn’t quite the word, but even on the plane, I got asked, ‘Would you like to see the landing?’ I went, ‘Yeah, great.’ So, it was jungle. It’s thick African forest. And it was cloudy. There’s a mist over it all. And the pilots are talking to each other. They say, ‘I don’t know, can you see the airport?’ Because they obviously didn’t have instruments. And one of them is going, ‘Is that it over there?’ Anyway, they landed. I think they went around a few times, but they found it and landed. So we had to get used to this kind of thing.
Paul McCartney
Wings: The Story Of A Band On The Run

The McCartneys overestimated the extent to which Lagos had been developed, and were shocked by the rudimentary facilities at EMI’s studio at 7 Wharf Road. They had received inoculations for several tropical diseases before leaving London, and had to take anti-malarial tablets during their time in Nigeria.

A car met the McCartneys at Lagos International Airport and took them to a villa complex in the Ikeja district, around 13 miles from the studio. They and their children shared one villa, with Laine and Emerick in another, approximately a mile away. Emerick switched soon after to a hotel in the city centre, having found the abundance of lizards and spiders too much to handle.
